headquarters: Sofia Tech Park, Labs Building, 111J Tsarigradsko Shose, Sofia, Bulgaria
description: MClimate is a Bulgarian IoT company building smart building technology for energy efficiency and sustainability. They design and manufacture LoRaWAN-based sensors and controllers for HVAC optimization, indoor air quality monitoring, water leak prevention, and energy management. With 400,000+ devices delivered across 2,500+ buildings in 60+ international markets, they serve commercial real estate, hospitality, social housing, and smart city sectors. Their product line includes hardware devices and MClimate Enterprise, a cloud SaaS platform for fleet management and analytics.

risks_and_known_vulnerabilities: CRITICAL: Single-source dependency on STMicroelectronics STM32 MCU — used in ALL 16 LoRaWAN products. 2021-2022 chip shortage caused industry-wide 6-12 month delivery delays. No drop-in alternative exists.
CRITICAL: Semtech LoRa transceiver has ZERO alternatives — Semtech holds the LoRa modulation patent. If Semtech has supply issues, the entire LoRaWAN product line stops.
HIGH: CTO (Nickole Dimitrova) likely holds deep knowledge of firmware architecture and LoRaWAN protocol implementation — bus factor risk for embedded systems expertise.
HIGH: Milan Stefanov (Chief Hardware Engineer) oversees all hardware design and 2 production facilities — concentration of hardware knowledge in one person.
HIGH: Primary production facility handles majority of manufacturing volume — disruption would severely impact delivery capacity with limited secondary facility backup.
MEDIUM: MClimate Enterprise cloud platform is single-region — outage would affect all 2,500+ buildings' monitoring and control capabilities.
MEDIUM: Vicki alone represents ~40% of revenue — product concentration risk if market shifts from radiator heating.
MEDIUM: Company is heavily dependent on LoRaWAN protocol standard — if market shifts to competing IoT protocols (Matter, Thread, 5G IoT), entire product strategy needs pivoting.
LOW-MEDIUM: 60+ international markets but sales team of 6 — key regional relationships may depend on individual salespeople.
LOW: Solar-powered device series (2023) uses novel light-harvesting technology — long-term field reliability not yet proven across all deployment conditions.
